intervention_label: CLAG-M (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, mitoxantrone, G-CSF)
intervention_dose: Cladribine 5 mg/m2, cytarabine 2 g/m2, mitoxantrone 10 mg/m2 and G-CSF; a second course given for partial response
population_detail: 118 registered patients from 11 Polish centres: 78 primary resistant, 40 relapsed. No post-allogeneic-HCT subgroup is reported and the study closed before venetoclax existed. WBC >10 g/L and age >34 predicted failure.
design: Multicentre phase 2, single-arm (Polish Adult Leukemia Group)
outcome: Complete remission after one or two CLAG-M courses
median_dor_or_pfs: 4-year disease-free survival 30% (95% CI 11-49) among the 66 patients in CR

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: true CR by the era's morphologic criteria, 66/118, after one or two courses

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: CR 53% plus partial remission 9% after course 1, per full text

safety_summary: Myelosuppression dominated: in patients reaching CR, neutrophils stayed below 0.5 g/L for a median 24 days and platelets below 20 g/L for 23 days. Severe infection hit 45%, and 8 of 118 died early, five of them from febrile neutropenia and sepsis.

toxicities.notes: 5 febrile neutropenia/sepsis, 1 CNS haemorrhage, 1 myocardial infarction
median duration 24 days (range 13-35) in patients achieving CR
median duration 23 days (range 15-104) in patients achieving CR

notes: One of the few true-CR figures in this dossier rather than a composite, and the largest. It predates venetoclax and reports no post-allograft subgroup, so 58% is not her number. AE terms came from the Wiley full text after the PubMed abstract gave only a narrative line; the 2008 study predates trial registration, so there is no ClinicalTrials.gov AE tab.

intervention_label: CLAG (cladribine, cytarabine, G-CSF) versus MEC
intervention_dose: Institutional CLAG and MEC schedules; doses not specified in the report
population_detail: 162 patients treated at a single centre, 97 CLAG and 65 MEC, split by primary refractory versus first relapse. Neither prior allogeneic HCT nor prior venetoclax is analysed.
outcome: Complete response rate, CLAG versus MEC
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 7.3 months CLAG versus 4.5 months MEC (p=0.05)
safety_summary: The published report carries no adverse-event table and no early-mortality figure; toxicity is not addressed beyond the efficacy comparison.
notes: The only head-to-head remission comparison between two deliverable salvage backbones here, and both rates are true CR. Toxicity: PubMed abstract has none, no PMC record, the study is a retrospective chart review with no NCT registration and so no ClinicalTrials.gov AE tab, and the Elsevier page is subscription-only; the four-page report appears to contain no AE table.

intervention_label: MEC (mitoxantrone, etoposide, cytarabine)
intervention_dose: Institutional MEC schedule, July 2014 to September 2022
population_detail: 60 adults treated at one centre. Response tracked against baseline disease burden: marrow blasts at or below 20% and peripheral blasts at or below 30% more than doubled the odds of CR/CRi. This patient sits at roughly 85% marrow and 82% peripheral blasts, the wrong side of both cut-points.
outcome: Complete remission (reported separately from CRi)
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 6.3 months; median time from MEC to CR/CRi 7.7 weeks

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: composite CR/CRi, the paper's primary endpoint

safety_summary: Febrile neutropenia, infection and severe oral mucositis were the common events; the paper gives rates for none of them. 21 of 60 patients (35%) went to intensive care during the admission.

toxicities.notes: described as common; no rate published in the abstract
described as common; no rate published in the abstract

notes: Splits CR from CRi, which most salvage series do not, and the blast-burden gradient argues directly against MEC at her disease load. Per-term AE rates: not in the PubMed abstract, no PMC deposit, no NCT registration for this retrospective cohort, and ScienceDirect returned 403; the ICU-transfer figure is the only quantified safety datum available.

intervention_label: Venetoclax plus high-dose cytarabine and mitoxantrone (RELAX)
intervention_dose: Venetoclax 400 mg orally days 1-14 after 3-day ramp-up, mitoxantrone 10 mg/m2 days 5-7, cytarabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily days 3-5 at the recommended phase 2 dose
indication: Relapsed or refractory AML in patients fit for intensive chemotherapy
population_detail: 55 patients, median age 57, ECOG 0-2, adequate hepatic and renal function. Entry required haematological relapse from first or second CR, or no response after one or two standard induction courses; 19 (35%) had a prior allogeneic HCT and 25 (45%) had ELN 2022 adverse risk. Second-salvage failure of intensive chemotherapy plus venetoclax, which is this patient's state, falls outside those entry criteria.
outcome: Composite complete remission rate by intention to treat
median_dor_or_pfs: Median follow-up 30.8 months (IQR 26.6-34.1)

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: composite CR/CRi, 41/55, ITT; the paper publishes no CR-only split

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: MRD-negative by flow among patients in composite remission; 41% by RT-PCR

safety_summary: Commonest all-grade events were febrile neutropenia 53%, pneumonia 22% and sepsis 22%. Fifteen serious adverse events occurred in 14 patients, mostly sepsis and pneumonia, and four deaths were judged potentially treatment-related (three sepsis, one pneumonia).

toxicities.notes: 15 events in 14 patients; the paper prints 13%, which does not reconcile with 14/55
potentially related: sepsis n=3, pneumonia n=1

notes: The highest remission figure among deliverable chemotherapy backbones and the one with the most post-transplant patients, but 75% is composite CR/CRi and no CR-only rate exists. Per-term grade 3+ rates: the abstract gives all-grade only, PMC13114347 holds a commentary rather than the full text, and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04330820 has hasResults=false, so the all-grade figures above are what the sources carry.

intervention_label: CPX-351 plus venetoclax
intervention_dose: CPX-351 at daunorubicin 44 mg/m2 days 1, 3, 5 with venetoclax 300 mg days 2-8 (recommended phase 2 dose, level -2)
indication: Relapsed or refractory AML in patients fit for intensive chemotherapy
population_detail: 33 patients, median age 58. Prior venetoclax was allowed and 58% had it; 44% were in second salvage or later; 30% had a prior transplant; adverse cytogenetics in 51%, myelodysplasia-related mutations in 64%, TP53-mutated 21%. Closest published match to her prior-therapy history in this dossier.
outcome: Complete remission, reported separately from the composite
median_dor_or_pfs: 2-year OS 49% (95% CI 23-100) in the first-salvage TP53-wild-type subgroup, 16% in the rest

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.subgroup: second salvage or later, or TP53-mutated

safety_summary: Myelosuppression drove the profile: grade 3+ febrile neutropenia in 76%, bacteraemia 64%, pneumonia 27%. Six grade 5 events (infection, haemorrhage, perforation, respiratory failure); 30-day mortality 9% and 60-day 21%.
notes: The cleanest published quantification of the gap she falls into: CRc 70% in first salvage with wild-type TP53 against 26% in second salvage or TP53-mutated, from one protocol with one response definition. True CR across the whole cohort was 15%, not the 39% composite. Safety and subgroup detail from PMC12510378.

intervention_label: Uproleselan (GMI-1271) added to MEC
intervention_dose: Uproleselan 10 mg/kg twice daily (recommended phase 2 dose) with mitoxantrone, etoposide and cytarabine
population_detail: 54 R/R patients treated at the recommended phase 2 dose (47 in expansion plus phase 1 patients dosed at that level); 66 R/R patients overall. Prior stem-cell transplantation was allowed and 12 (18%) of the R/R cohort had one. E-selectin ligand expression above 10% predicted higher response.
outcome: Complete remission at the recommended phase 2 dose, reported separately from CRi
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 8.8 months (95% CI 5.7-11.4)
safety_summary: Grade 3+ febrile neutropenia 59%, thrombocytopenia 35%, sepsis 12%; mucositis was strikingly low at 2%, which is the regimen's selling point next to MEC alone. Induction mortality was low at 2% by day 30 and 9% by day 60.
notes: Reports CR apart from the composite, which is what this question needs, and 18% of the R/R cohort had a prior transplant. The confirmatory phase 3 in R/R AML did not convert the signal, so the agent is not a deliverable route now. Safety and denominators from PMC11017789.

intervention_label: Lintuzumab-Ac225 (225Ac anti-CD33) after CLAG-M
intervention_dose: Lintuzumab-Ac225 0.25-1.0 microCi/kg 7 (+2) days after CLAG-M days 1-6; recommended phase 2 dose 0.75 microCi/kg
population_detail: 26 patients (21 in 3+3 escalation, 5 at the RP2D); 86.7% of evaluable patients had high-risk disease. Separate readouts for the TP53-mutated and prior-venetoclax subgroups, both single-digit in size.
outcome: Composite complete remission (CR/CRi)
median_dor_or_pfs: Estimated 1-year PFS 30.8% (95% CI 14.6-48.5)

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: composite CR/CRi in evaluable patients; no CR-only split published

safety_summary: Grade 3/4 febrile neutropenia 65.4% and white-cell decrease 50%, described by the authors as what CLAG-M plus an alpha emitter would be expected to produce.
notes: Best subgroup numbers on two of her three hardest axes, and every one of them is composite CR/CRi with no CR-only split and single-digit denominators. Not deliverable: the trial completed and the follow-on NCT06802523 is suspended. Extraction carried from the reference-verified row ce-x7q2r2-016 in the source case; abstract-level safety only.

intervention_label: Fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin monotherapy (MyloFrance-1)
intervention_dose: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7, one course
population_detail: 57 patients in first relapse, no prior allogeneic transplant, no prior venetoclax. Response tracked with P-glycoprotein and MRP1 efflux activity rather than CD33 density.
outcome: Complete remission
median_dor_or_pfs: Median relapse-free survival 11 months
safety_summary: Neutropenia below 500/microL lasted a median 23 days and thrombocytopenia below 50,000/microL 21 days. No grade 3-4 liver toxicity and no veno-occlusive disease, including in the seven patients transplanted afterwards.
notes: A clean CR figure with CRp broken out separately, and the reason fractionated dosing can precede a transplant without veno-occlusive disease. First relapse, transplant-naive, venetoclax-naive, so 26% is a ceiling rather than an estimate for her. Extraction carried from the reference-verified row ce-x7q2r2-017 in the source case.

intervention_label: Hypomethylating agent plus venetoclax for post-allograft relapse
intervention_dose: Azacitidine or decitabine with venetoclax, institutional dosing
indication: AML or MDS relapsing after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 83 patients (69 AML, 14 MDS) relapsing after allograft, median time to relapse 7.0 months. 55% had prior venetoclax exposure and 28% of those had already failed a venetoclax regimen; prior venetoclax failure did not predict worse survival. Response was assessed on marrow, with no extramedullary reporting.
outcome: Composite complete response (CR or CRi)

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: composite CR/CRi, 40/83; the paper does not split CR from CRi

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: 20 patients went on to a second allogeneic HCT; 7 more (8%) received DLI alone

safety_summary: Almost universal cytopenias (grade 3-4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia both 99%, mostly grade 4) with febrile neutropenia in 24%, but only three deaths within 30 days, all from infection.
notes: Closest published population to hers on the transplant axis, and the only one where prior venetoclax failure was tested against outcome and did not predict it. The 48% is composite CR/CRi with no CR-only split, and marrow-only assessment leaves her thigh lesion unaddressed. Safety and subgroup detail from PMC13396606.

intervention_label: Venetoclax-based salvage for post-transplant AML relapse
intervention_dose: Venetoclax with an HMA or low-dose cytarabine, off-label institutional dosing
population_detail: 21 patients transplanted for myeloid disease who relapsed with AML, 19 evaluable for response. Median age 64.5, median time from HCT to relapse 5.7 months. Antecedent haematologic malignancy in 6, complex karyotype in 6, TP53 mutations in 5 of 21 — a risk profile that overlaps hers closely.
outcome: Complete remission, reported separately from CRi
median_dor_or_pfs: Nine patients held response for 3 months or more; 8 were still on therapy at data cut

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: composite CR/CRi, 8/19 (5 CR + 3 CRi); no partial responses

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: four further patients reached morphologic leukaemia-free state

safety_summary: The report describes no per-term adverse-event table and gives no early-mortality figure.
notes: One of the few post-transplant venetoclax series that separates CR from CRi: 5 of 19, not the 42.1% composite. Toxicity: no AE table in the PubMed abstract, no PMC deposit, no NCT registration for this retrospective series, and the Wiley page is subscription-only.

intervention_label: Venetoclax combinations across treatment settings including post-allograft relapse
intervention_dose: Venetoclax orally in 28-day cycles with an HMA or low-dose cytarabine
indication: Newly diagnosed, relapsed or refractory AML, including relapse after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 56 consecutive patients treated 2019-2021, split into first-line, subsequent-line R/R without prior allograft, and relapse after allogeneic HCT. The post-allograft group is the relevant one here; its exact size is not stated in the abstract.
journal: Journal of Cancer Research and Clinical Oncology
outcome: Overall response (composite complete remission plus partial remission)
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 4.0 months from venetoclax start in the post-allograft group

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: composite CR plus partial remission; CR is not reported separately

safety_summary: Haematological events dominated: grade 3-4 neutropenia in 44.6% and thrombocytopenia in 14.5% of the whole 56-patient cohort.
notes: A third post-allograft venetoclax datapoint, and the weakest of the three: 42.8% pools complete and partial remission, so it cannot be read against a CR bar at all. Kept as triangulation on the post-transplant axis, not as a CR estimate.

intervention_label: Salvage therapy after failure of venetoclax-based treatment
intervention_dose: Mixed physician's-choice salvage; six patients received venetoclax plus actinomycin D with or without low-dose cytarabine
indication: Relapsed or refractory AML after failure of venetoclax-based salvage
population_detail: 28 heavily pretreated patients (median 3 prior lines, range 2-6), 16 (57%) previously allografted, 20 (71%) ECOG 2-4, 18 (64%) ELN 2017 adverse risk. 22 received a post-venetoclax salvage regimen; the remaining 6 were too unwell to treat.
outcome: Overall response (complete remission plus morphologic leukaemia-free state)
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 3.9 months overall; 4.3 months with salvage versus 1.3 months with palliative care alone (p<0.001)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: pools CR with morphologic leukaemia-free state; no CR-only rate for the whole salvaged group

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.subgroup: venetoclax plus actinomycin D with or without low-dose cytarabine

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: median with salvage versus 1.3 months palliative care

safety_summary: No adverse-event table is published; the authors note that six of 28 patients were too unwell for any salvage attempt, which is itself the tolerability signal.
notes: The pessimistic anchor for her exact axis: 23% response after venetoclax salvage failure, and that figure pools CR with MLFS rather than reporting CR alone. Toxicity: none in the PubMed abstract, no PMC deposit, retrospective and unregistered so no ClinicalTrials.gov AE tab, Wiley page subscription-only.

intervention_label: Idasanutlin plus cytarabine versus cytarabine alone (MIRROS)
intervention_dose: Idasanutlin 300 mg orally twice daily or placebo, with cytarabine 1 g/m2 IV days 1-5 of 28-day cycles
indication: Relapsed or refractory AML after up to two prior induction regimens
population_detail: 447 adults randomised 2:1 regardless of TP53 status, ECOG 0-2; the CR analysis below is the 355-patient TP53 wild-type ITT population (232 idasanutlin, 123 placebo). Roughly 15% of all-comers were TP53-mutant but no separate response rate is published for them.
outcome: Complete remission rate, idasanutlin-cytarabine versus placebo-cytarabine
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 8.3 versus 9.1 months (HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.81-1.45, p=0.58)

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.subgroup: idasanutlin plus cytarabine, TP53 wild-type ITT
outcomes.notes: true CR, 47/232; odds ratio 1.23 (95% CI 0.70-2.18) versus control

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.subgroup: placebo plus cytarabine, TP53 wild-type ITT
outcomes.notes: true CR, 21/123 — the cytarabine-alone CR benchmark in R/R AML

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: CR + CRp + CRi; control 22.0%, OR 2.25 (95% CI 1.36-3.72)

safety_summary: Grade 3+ diarrhoea 16.9% versus 6.2% and sepsis 11.3% versus 4.8% marked the idasanutlin arm; febrile neutropenia was similar (52.5% versus 49.3%). 30-day mortality 7.9% versus 5.5%.
notes: Carried for its control arm rather than its experimental one: 17.1% true CR with intermediate-dose cytarabine alone is the largest randomised CR benchmark in R/R AML in this file, and the idasanutlin arm did not beat it. Response and AE detail from PMC9327534.

intervention_label: 131I-apamistamab (Iomab-B) targeted radioimmunoconditioning before allogeneic HCT (SIERRA)
intervention_dose: Dosimetry-guided therapeutic 131I-apamistamab infusion followed by reduced-intensity conditioning and allogeneic HCT
indication: Active relapsed or refractory AML, age 55 and over
population_detail: 153 randomised (76 apamistamab, 77 conventional care), all with active disease. Prior allogeneic or autologous HSCT was an exclusion, so this patient could not have enrolled. The endpoint is CR durable to 180 days, a stricter bar than a single marrow assessment.
comparator: Conventional salvage care with allo-HCT if CR/CRp achieved; crossover permitted
outcome: Durable complete remission lasting 180 days
median_dor_or_pfs: Durable CR by definition lasted at least 180 days

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: durable CR to 180 days, ITT — a stricter definition than a single-timepoint CR

safety_summary: Grade 3+ treatment-related events 59.7% versus 59.2%, essentially identical between arms. 100-day non-relapse mortality 12.2% versus 14.3%; treatment-related deaths 3 versus 4.
notes: Randomised evidence that antigen-targeted conditioning can carry active leukaemia into a graft where salvage produced no durable CR at all. Prior HCT was an exclusion, so it cannot supply her a rate; and the 17.1% is a 180-day durable CR, not comparable to the single-assessment CRs elsewhere in this file. Extraction carried from the reference-verified row ce-x7q2r2-027 in the source case.

intervention_label: FLAMSA sequential conditioning into reduced-intensity allogeneic HCT with prophylactic DLI
intervention_dose: Fludarabine 30 mg/m2, cytarabine 2 g/m2, amsacrine 100 mg/m2 for 4 days; after 3 days rest, 4 Gy TBI plus ATG plus cyclophosphamide 80-120 mg/kg; prophylactic DLI from day +120
indication: High-risk AML and MDS including progressive or refractory disease
population_detail: 75 consecutive patients, median age 52.3; 59 had progressive or refractory disease and 49% of informative patients had unfavourable karyotype. 31 had HLA-identical sibling donors. Overwhelmingly first transplants, and the series predates venetoclax-era salvage by two decades.
outcome: Complete remission after sequential conditioning
median_dor_or_pfs: 2-year overall survival 42%, leukaemia-free survival 40%

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: true CR, 66/75 — but produced by the whole transplant procedure, not by chemotherapy alone

safety_summary: No per-term adverse-event table is published; outcome was driven by non-relapse mortality and GVHD, with survival best in patients receiving high CD34+ doses and having limited GVHD.
notes: The highest true-CR figure in the file, and the one whose denominator is least like her: mostly first transplants, refractory disease, pre-venetoclax. Its argument is that remission can be a product of conditioning rather than a prerequisite for it. Toxicity: PubMed abstract and JCO page report NRM and GVHD narratively with no per-term AE table, and the 2005 study predates registration so there is no ClinicalTrials.gov AE tab.

intervention_label: Watchful waiting into immediate allogeneic HCT versus high-dose cytarabine remission induction (ASAP)
intervention_dose: Control arm: cytarabine 3 g/m2 twice daily days 1-3 (1 g/m2 if over 60 or comorbid) plus mitoxantrone 10 mg/m2 days 3-5. Experimental arm: disease control only, then conditioning
indication: Non-favourable-risk AML not in CR after first induction, or untreated first relapse
population_detail: 281 patients aged 18-75 with a donor available. Prior allogeneic HCT was not part of this population, and entry was first relapse or failure of first induction, not second-salvage venetoclax-refractory disease. The endpoint is CR on day 56 after transplant, not CR from chemotherapy.
comparator: Remission induction with high-dose cytarabine plus mitoxantrone
outcome: Treatment success, defined as complete remission on day 56 after allogeneic HCT

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: CR on day 56 post-transplant, 116/140; non-inferiority not shown at the pre-specified 2.5% level

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: ITT difference favouring disease control; per-protocol 2.7% (-6.3 to 11.8)

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: grade 3+ non-haematological AEs, 30/140, versus 61% (86/141) with induction

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: median hospital days between randomisation and HCT, versus 42 days with induction

safety_summary: Grade 3+ non-haematological adverse events were 21% with watchful waiting versus 61% with induction. Between randomisation and conditioning, two patients per arm died of progressive AML; two treatment-related deaths occurred with induction and none with disease control.

toxicities.term: Death from progressive AML before conditioning

notes: The one randomised test of whether inducing CR before transplant is worth doing, and the answer was that it bought nothing measurable while costing 40 points of grade 3+ non-haematological toxicity and 27 hospital days. Formally inapplicable to her — prior allograft was not in this population — but it is the strongest evidence in the file that maximising CR before transplant may be the wrong goal. Read the statistics precisely: non-inferiority was not shown at the 2.5% level (p=0.036), and induction was not better either.

intervention_label: Pivekimab sunirine (IMGN632), CD123-directed antibody-drug conjugate
intervention_dose: 0.045 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (recommended phase 2 dose)
population_detail: 91 enrolled overall, 68 on the every-3-week schedule; the efficacy estimate is the 29 patients at the recommended phase 2 dose. ECOG 0-1 required, which she meets. CD123 positivity needed no density threshold, which suits her qualitative-only flow.
design: First-in-human phase 1/2 dose escalation and expansion (NCT03386513)
outcome: Composite complete remission at the recommended phase 2 dose
safety_summary: At the recommended dose the commonest grade 3+ related events were febrile neutropenia 10%, infusion reactions 7% and anaemia 7%. Two dose-limiting veno-occlusive disease events occurred in escalation, both reversible; one treatment-related death.
notes: Single-agent CD123 targeting with a composite CR of 17% and a confidence interval running from 6 to 36 — too wide and too low to compete on this question's endpoint. Veno-occlusive disease matters for anyone heading to a second graft. Extraction carried from the reference-verified row ce-x7q2r2-011 in the source case.

intervention_label: Flotetuzumab (CD123 x CD3 bispecific DART) in TP53-abnormal R/R AML
intervention_dose: 500 ng/kg/day continuous infusion
indication: Relapsed or refractory AML with TP53 mutation or 17p deletion
population_detail: 15 of 45 flotetuzumab-treated patients with marrow transcriptomic profiling carried TP53 mutations or 17p deletion. Post-hoc subgroup, and the response definition is under 5% marrow blasts rather than ELN CR with count recovery.
design: Correlative analysis nested in a phase 1/2 trial (NCT02152956)
outcome: Response defined as under 5% marrow blasts in TP53-abnormal R/R AML
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 10.3 months among TP53-abnormal responders (range 3.3-21.3)

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: 7/15 reaching <5% marrow blasts; this is not ELN CR and count recovery was not required

notes: The strongest TP53-specific remission signal anywhere in this dossier and the most stranded: 15 patients, post-hoc, a non-ELN response definition, and a discontinued drug. Safety: the correlative paper carries no safety section (checked PubMed abstract and PMC7594389); parent-trial toxicity sits with the Uy 2021 report.

intervention_label: Second-salvage therapy in AML (pooled regimens)
intervention_dose: Mixed: allogeneic SCT in 74, high-dose cytarabine combinations in 171, standard-dose cytarabine combinations in 30, non-cytarabine combinations in 73, phase 1-2 single agents in 246
population_detail: 594 patients treated at a single centre 1980-2004, median age 50. Adverse factors for CR were first CR under 6 months, second CR under 6 months, salvage not including allogeneic SCT, non-inv(16) disease, platelets under 50 x10^9/L and WBC over 50 x10^9/L. Marrow blasts at or above 50% was an adverse factor for survival — she is at roughly 85%.
outcome: Complete remission rate at second salvage
median_dor_or_pfs: Median CR duration 7 months; median survival 1.5 months, 1-year survival 8%

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: true CR, 76/594, across all second-salvage regimens

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: true CR; no patient in this group remitted

safety_summary: No adverse-event data are reported; the analysis covers response and survival only.
notes: The number that recalibrates every first-salvage figure in this file: 13% true CR once a patient is at second salvage, with risk-group rates from 54% down to zero. She carries at least the non-inv(16) and salvage-without-transplant factors, and her long first remission counts in her favour. Toxicity: none published; the paper is a pre-registration-era retrospective with no PMC deposit and no NCT record.

intervention_label: Salvage therapy in R/R AML with newly detected TP53 mutation
intervention_dose: Mixed intensive and lower-intensity salvage regimens
indication: Relapsed or refractory AML with a TP53 mutation acquired during therapy
population_detail: 200 patients with TP53 wild-type AML at diagnosis who later relapsed or were refractory; 29 (15%) had a newly detectable TP53 mutation, median VAF 15% (range 1.1-95.6). Emergence was more common after intensive therapy (23% vs 10%) and after transplant (36% vs 12%) — which is her exact history.
outcome: Composite complete remission by TP53 variant allele frequency
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 4.6 months after acquiring the TP53 mutation; 1-year OS 19%
safety_summary: No adverse-event reporting; the analysis is of mutation emergence, response and survival.
notes: Bears directly on her unresolved TP53 in both directions: 36% of post-transplant patients acquired a TP53 mutation that was not there at diagnosis, and remission odds tracked variant burden (composite CR/CRi 41% below 20% VAF versus 13% at or above). It argues for resolving the variant with a quantitative assay rather than accepting a negative from a 2%-LOD panel. Toxicity: this is a mutation-emergence and outcome analysis with no AE reporting in the abstract or the AJH full text, and no NCT registration for the retrospective cohort.

intervention_label: Intensive chemotherapy, HMA-venetoclax or HMA alone in TP53-mutated AML
intervention_dose: Pooled across 12 studies: intensive chemotherapy, venetoclax plus HMA, or HMA alone
population_detail: 17 publications describing 12 studies, all in untreated TP53-mutated AML. Frontline only, so these are ceilings for a refractory second-salvage patient rather than estimates.
design: Systematic review and meta-analysis with random-effects pooling
outcome: Pooled complete remission rate by treatment class
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 6.5 months intensive chemotherapy, 6.2 months venetoclax-HMA, 6.1 months HMA

outcomes.name: DoR
outcomes.notes: venetoclax-HMA 5.0 months; not reported for HMA

safety_summary: The meta-analysis pools efficacy endpoints only and reports no safety outcomes.
notes: Useful mainly as the TP53 branch's upper bound and for one contrast the composite hides: intensive chemotherapy and venetoclax-HMA look equivalent on CR/CRi (46% vs 49%) but not on true CR (43% vs 33%). Every figure is frontline and treatment-naive, so none of it transfers to her line. Toxicity: the meta-analysis pooled efficacy endpoints only; no AE extraction was performed by its authors, so there is nothing to carry (checked abstract and PMC9990239).

intervention_label: Intensive chemotherapy programmes (FLAI, HDAC-IDA, HyperCVAD, MEC) for myeloid sarcoma
intervention_dose: Institutional FLAI, high-dose cytarabine plus idarubicin, HyperCVAD or MEC schedules
population_detail: 48 patients from 9 Italian centres, median age 46: 9 isolated extramedullary, 24 de novo AML-related, 15 secondary-AML-related — the last being the category her thigh lesion falls into. 43 (90%) received an intensive programme; 22 (46%) were transplanted. Response is reported as CR without separating marrow from extramedullary assessment.
outcome: Complete remission after intensive chemotherapy
median_dor_or_pfs: Median OS 16.7 months for the whole cohort; 18 months with an intensive programme versus 5 months without

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: CR across intensively treated patients; the paper does not state whether extramedullary sites were separately assessed at response

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: median; 5 months without an intensive programme

safety_summary: Death during induction was 5% among the 43 intensively treated patients; no other adverse-event data are published.
notes: The largest adult myeloid sarcoma series with a remission figure attached, and it still cannot tell you whether the sarcoma responded: CR is reported without splitting marrow from extramedullary assessment. Secondary-AML-related myeloid sarcoma, her category, had the worst survival of the three groups. Toxicity: only the 5% induction-death rate is published; no PMC deposit, no registration, Elsevier page subscription-only.

intervention_label: Systemic therapy for myeloid sarcoma including venetoclax-HMA
intervention_dose: Pooled across studies; the venetoclax arm is venetoclax with a hypomethylating agent
population_detail: 85 studies, 7241 patients; mutational concordance assessed in 112 with paired myeloid-sarcoma and marrow sequencing. 56% of paired cases showed discordant mutation profiles between the sarcoma and the marrow, which is the mechanistic reason a marrow CR need not mean an extramedullary CR.
outcome: Response rate to venetoclax plus hypomethylating agent in myeloid sarcoma
median_dor_or_pfs: Pooled median overall survival 12.8 months

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: pooled response rate, mainly in secondary myeloid sarcoma; the pooled definition is not resolved to CR

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: discordant mutation profiles between myeloid sarcoma tissue and marrow

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: isolated extramedullary relapse among relapsing post-transplant patients

safety_summary: The review pools clinical, molecular and outcome data and reports no safety outcomes.
notes: Two findings carry into her case: molecular discordance between sarcoma and marrow in 56% of paired samples, and isolated extramedullary relapse in 46% of post-transplant relapses. Both say a marrow CR cannot be assumed to cover the thigh. The 44% venetoclax-HMA figure is a pooled response rate across heterogeneous reports, not a CR rate. Toxicity: the review pools clinical, molecular and survival data with no safety extraction (checked abstract and PMC12730967).

intervention_label: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin for CD33-positive extramedullary leukaemia
intervention_dose: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin, dosing not standardised across the two cases
population_detail: Two paediatric patients with CD33-positive extramedullary disease, followed with serial clinical examination and FDG-PET/CT. No denominators, no adult data, no marrow-versus-extramedullary response split beyond the imaging itself.
outcome: Clinical and radiographic response of extramedullary lesions

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: both showed reduction of extramedullary disease on clinical exam and FDG-PET/CT; neither response is graded as CR

safety_summary: No adverse-event data are reported for either patient.
notes: The only source found that measured an extramedullary CD33-positive lesion at response rather than assuming the marrow answer covered it — and it is two children with no CR grading. Worth naming for the imaging method (serial FDG-PET/CT) more than for the effect. Toxicity: neither case describes adverse events (checked the PubMed abstract; no PMC deposit; case series, so no registry record).

intervention_label: Pre-transplant MRD status versus active disease at myeloablative allogeneic HCT
intervention_dose: Myeloablative conditioning, peripheral blood or marrow graft
population_detail: 359 consecutive adults transplanted 2006-2014, staged by 10-colour multiparametric flow on marrow: 235 MRD-negative remission, 76 MRD-positive morphologic remission, 48 active AML. Any detectable level counted as MRD-positive. First transplants, not second.
comparator: MRD-negative remission versus MRD-positive remission versus active disease
outcome: Three-year relapse and overall survival by pre-transplant disease state
median_dor_or_pfs: 3-year OS 73% MRD-negative, 26% MRD-positive remission, 23% active disease
safety_summary: Transplant-related toxicity is not tabulated; the analysis compares relapse and survival by pre-transplant disease state.
notes: The answer to whether CR depth matters, and it is blunt: a morphologic CR that is MRD-positive performed like untreated active disease (3-year relapse 67% vs 65%, OS 26% vs 23%), while MRD-negative CR sat at 22% and 73%. If reinduction can only reach an MRD-positive CR, this cohort says the CR bought little. First transplants only, so the read-across to a second graft is an assumption. Toxicity: a pre-transplant staging analysis with no AE table (checked abstract and PMC4872033); GVHD and NRM are covered only inside the survival models.

intervention_label: Consolidation chemotherapy to deepen remission before allogeneic HCT in AML CR2
intervention_dose: Institutional consolidation courses after achieving CR2, versus proceeding directly to transplant
indication: AML in second complete remission proceeding to allogeneic HCT
population_detail: 135 patients transplanted in CR2 at one centre 2015-2019: 72 consolidated, 63 not. A separate comparison pitted extra consolidation to reach MRD-negativity against immediate transplant while MRD-positive. All first transplants, predominantly haploidentical, in a Chinese single-centre population.
outcome: Five-year leukaemia-free and overall survival by pre-transplant consolidation
median_dor_or_pfs: 5-year LFS 72.7% with consolidation versus 62.7% without (p=0.15)

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: 5-year cumulative incidence of relapse; no consolidation 19.9%

safety_summary: No adverse-event table; the comparison covers relapse, non-relapse mortality and survival.
notes: Pulls the other way from a naive reading of Araki: chasing MRD-negativity with more chemotherapy before transplant did not measurably improve LFS or OS over transplanting MRD-positive. The population is patients already in CR2 heading to a first graft, so it speaks to how hard to push, not to whether to induce at all. Toxicity: no AE table in the paper (checked abstract and PMC12025703); non-relapse mortality is the only harm endpoint reported.

exclusion_reason: Endpoint is overall survival by prognostic score, not a remission rate; the index reports no CR rate for any risk group, so it cannot answer a CR question.
intervention_label: Prognostic index for AML in first relapse (Breems score)
notes: Read for whether the score could grade her remission odds. It grades survival, not remission, and it is built on first relapse in patients aged 15-60 from 1987-2004 trials.

exclusion_reason: Reports overall survival and DFS comparisons between transplant and chemotherapy in myeloid sarcoma with no complete-remission rate published.
intervention_label: Allogeneic HCT versus intensive chemotherapy in myeloid sarcoma
notes: Larger than the Lazzarotto series (162 patients, 12 centres) but survival-only, so it cannot carry the extramedullary CR axis. Its CR1-versus-non-CR1 stratification is about who benefits from transplant, not about inducing remission.

exclusion_reason: Population is newly diagnosed TP53-aberrant MDS and AML; the response rates are frontline and no relapsed/refractory CR rate is reported.
intervention_label: TP53 aberration burden and outcome in myeloid neoplasms
notes: Read for the TP53 high-risk versus low-risk allelic-burden split, which is the framework her pending variant call would slot into. Frontline population, and response is reported as OR and CRc without a true-CR breakdown.

exclusion_reason: Single case report; no denominator and no generalisable remission rate.
intervention_label: Venetoclax with hypomethylating agent then transplant for cervical myeloid sarcoma
notes: Read because it documents a PET-negative and MRD-negative pre-transplant remission covering both marrow and an extramedullary site, which is the response standard this question wants. One patient, so it cannot supply a rate.

exclusion_reason: Two case reports of venetoclax-HMA with dose-adjusted HAG; no denominator and no CR rate.
intervention_label: Venetoclax plus HMA with dose-adjusted HAG in R/R AML
notes: Surfaced on the post-venetoclax-failure search and read to check for a salvage cohort. Two patients, one of whom did not complete treatment.

exclusion_reason: Frontline therapy in core-binding-factor AML — a favourable-risk, treatment-naive population with no overlap with her disease or line.
intervention_label: CLAG-GO (cladribine, high-dose cytarabine, gemtuzumab ozogamicin) frontline in CBF-AML
notes: The only CLAG-GO efficacy publication found, and it is in the wrong disease. The CLAG-GO protocol she could actually enter (NCT04050280) still has no published results in refractory AML, so that arm of the trial screen rests on registry text alone.
